slots.writingObjective: State as a fact about TextOS that an observed source becomes usable evidence only after a person approves it for that article.
One sentence for a search result: in TextOS a person approves each piece of evidence for one article, under wording they validate, and can withdraw it.
Open on the CMO's worry — an AI writer that treats anything it found online as a fact about their brand — and say how TextOS answered it in October 2026, without the mechanism yet.
slots.buyerIntent: Will the writer use facts I never checked?

slots.heading: How does an AI writer end up using only facts you approved?
slots.writingObjective: Answer directly: a source the system observed is never presented as evidence; an identified person approves it for this article under wording they validate; only approved and usable evidence is offered to the writer.

slots.heading: Only a person can say yes
slots.writingObjective: Explain who may approve: a non-human identity is refused, the identity comes from the signed-in session and is never passed in by a caller, operator shortcuts are refused, and the approval is validated before anything is written.
slots.buyerIntent: Could an automated process approve on my behalf?

slots.heading: An approval belongs to one article and one wording
slots.writingObjective: Explain why an approval is narrow: it lapses when the quoted passage changes, it is not copied when a workspace is transferred, and withdrawing it removes the fact from writing and from the draft sent to WordPress.
slots.buyerIntent: What if the source changes or I change my mind?

slots.heading: Offered to the writer, never imposed
slots.writingObjective: Explain how approved evidence is used: offered to the short answer and to one body section that it fits, never to the opening or the next step, with no claim type forced on the writer; repeated wording is flagged and exact duplicates blocked.
slots.buyerIntent: Will one approved fact be repeated everywhere?

slots.heading: Choosing among approved facts, and saying why
slots.writingObjective: Explain the selection among approved evidence: deterministic, guided by relevance, coverage and specificity, keeping corroboration between independent sources, setting aside repetition of one source, stating gaps, and showing the reader why these facts were used without internal identifiers. End with what a candidate passage is: proposed, never approved or offered by itself.
